Toy Story 2, released in 1999, is a critically acclaimed animated film by Pixar Animation Studios that continues the adventures of Woody, Buzz Lightyear, and their toy companions. The film explores themes of loyalty, self-worth, and the meaning of family while expanding upon the world established in the original Toy Story.

The sequel follows Woody after he's stolen by a toy collector named Al, who recognizes him as a valuable collectible from a 1950s TV show called "Woody's Roundup." Through this storyline, we're introduced to new characters including Jessie the cowgirl, Stinky Pete the Prospector, and Bullseye the horse, who were all part of the same toy line as Woody.

The film's production was notably challenging, with Pixar nearly losing the entire movie due to a technical error that deleted 90% of the work files. Fortunately, a technical supervisor had backed up the film on her home computer, saving the project.

The movie was also groundbreaking for its time in terms of animation quality, particularly in the rendering of human characters and fabric textures. The film's success led to a partnership between Pixar and clothing manufacturer Gap, which produced a line of Woody's Roundup merchandise that became highly sought after by collectors.

Tom Hanks and Tim Allen reprised their roles as Woody and Buzz, while acclaimed actress Betty White joined the cast as Jessie, bringing her characteristic charm to the role. The film's soundtrack, composed by Randy Newman, went on to win both an Academy Award and a Golden Globe for Best Original Score.

Toy Story 2, released in 1999, is a beloved animated film that continues the adventures of Woody, Buzz Lightyear, and their fellow toys. The sequel expands upon the original's themes of friendship, loyalty, and identity while introducing compelling new characters.

The film follows Woody after he's stolen by Al, a toy collector who recognizes him as a valuable collectible from "Woody's Roundup," a 1950s TV show. This leads to Woody discovering his own history and meeting other Roundup toys, including Jessie the cowgirl, Stinky Pete the Prospector, and his trusty horse Bullseye.

Meanwhile, Buzz leads a rescue mission with other toys from Andy's room, including Rex, Hamm, Slinky Dog, and Mr. Potato Head. Their journey across the city provides many memorable moments, including the famous crossing of a busy street using traffic cones.

The film was originally planned as a direct-to-video release but was upgraded to a theatrical release due to its high quality during production. It went on to gross over $485 million worldwide and received universal acclaim from critics.

The movie's production was notably challenging, with Pixar having to completely restart animation halfway through when a technical error nearly erased all their work. Director John Lasseter stepped in during the final months of production, replacing the original director Brad Bird, who went on to direct The Iron Giant that same year. The film's soundtrack, composed by Thomas Newman, featured Randy Newman's "When She Loved Me," which won the Academy Award for Best Original Song in 2000.

"Toy Story 2," released in 1999, is a science fiction comedy-drama and one of the most highly praised animated films of the 20th century. Directed by Michael Bay, the movie continues the adventures of Woody, Buzz Lightyear, and their toy friends. In this sequel, Woody is kidnapped by a toy collector named Al McWhiggin, who plans to sell him to a toy museum in Japan. Buzz and the other toys embark on a daring rescue mission to save Woody before he is shipped overseas.

An interesting fact about the film is that it was originally planned to be a direct-to-video sequel, but due to its impressive storyline and Pixar's new CGI technology, Disney decided to release it theatrically. The film broke record sales, becoming the highest-grossing animated film of the time, surpassing the success of its predecessor, "The Lion King."

The film was also notable for introducing new characters like Jessie, Bullseye, and Emperor Zurg, Buzz Lightyear's long-lost brother. It also features the popular song "You've Got a Friend in Me," performed by karaoke legend, Ricky Martin. All these factors contributed to "Toy Story 2" earning several Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Best Original Score.

"Toy Story 2" is a 1999 American computer-animated film produced by Pixar Animation Studios and released by Walt Disney Pictures. It is the sequel to the 1995 film "Toy Story" and the second installment in the Toy Story franchise. Directed by John Lasseter, co-directed by Lee Unkrich and Ash Brannon, the film continues the adventures of Woody, Buzz Lightyear, and the rest of the toy gang.

In "Toy Story 2," Woody is stolen by a toy collector named Al McWhiggin, who plans to sell him to a museum in Japan. Buzz and the other toys embark on a rescue mission to save Woody. Meanwhile, Woody discovers his origins as a collectible from a popular 1950s TV show called "Woody's Roundup" and meets other characters from the show, including Jessie, Bullseye, and Stinky Pete the Prospector.

The film explores themes of identity, friendship, and the fear of being forgotten. It was highly praised for its animation, story, and character development, and it was a commercial success. "Toy Story 2" received several awards and nominations, including a Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy. It is often regarded as one of the best animated sequels ever made.
